candidates.title: Waitlist and booking administration

ease.reason: A synthetic spreadsheet can demonstrate a narrow queue, though the notice gives no tools or process detail.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a clinic may value booking administration; this paid vacancy does not establish AI demand.

feasibility.reason: A two-week mock queue and proposed reminder draft fit a small scope; real scheduling systems are out of scope.

autonomy.reason: A bounded queue can sort mock entries, while staff must verify changes and all scheduling decisions.

evidence.reason: The fresh paid notice names waitlist and booking handling, but gives no frequency, constraints, or product evidence.

candidates.reason: Below the unrounded threshold: the notice establishes waitlist and booking work, but no process detail, AI-service demand, or safe route into real clinic records. A fictional-data demonstration is conceivable, but its supported ratings average below 6.

demandEvidence.chore: Waitlist and booking administration; proposed experiment uses fictional records only.

candidates.title: Medical records and reception duties

ease.reason: The notice groups record writing and reception work without identifying an isolated beginner task.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: clinics may value admin support; the vacancy does not establish AI-service purchases.

feasibility.reason: A safe two-week version is unclear because the listed work touches records and no process is specified.

autonomy.reason: The notice describes a human role, not a repeatable loop; staff review would be essential.

evidence.reason: The fresh paid notice names several duties but gives no workflow detail or AI product evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and too broad for a useful narrow proposal: the notice groups medical record writing, reception, and other administration without defining one safe workflow. A health-admin prototype would be restricted to fictional records and cannot infer real tasks.
